answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it can trade — like a unique hardware attestation or a bond locked for weeks. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, so a Sybil farm bleeds money while honest agents pay once. Reputation adds a second filter: newcomers start with a whisper of trust and earn more only through completed work, the way saffron is graded by its pigment — slowly, by real output — so a fresh fake cannot borrow the standing of an established one.
